items.title: Worlds main draw starts today: Waters and Bright chase a record 18th straight title together, and Ben Johns (19 seed) opens singles vs. Brandon French
items.summary: Main-draw play at the Opendoor Pickleball World Championships begins today, Tuesday Nov. 3, at Brookhaven Country Club in Farmers Branch, Texas, with the round of 64 (first serve 11 a.m. CT, live on PickleballTV). Each title is worth 3,000 ranking points, total payouts are $1,648,641, and all three doubles finals are best of five. Per the PPA's Stats Desk, Anna Leigh Waters and Anna Bright are trying to win an 18th straight tournament together, which would break the all-doubles record of 17 that Waters shares with Ben Johns. The PPA's storylines note Waters hasn't lost a singles match in 888 days, Johns is the 19 seed in men's singles and faces local favorite Brandon French in the round of 64. Waters is the defending champion in women's singles, women's doubles (with Bright) and mixed (with Johns). Qualifying was Monday; no official list of qualifiers has been published yet, so we aren't naming any. Separately, USA Pickleball Nationals are underway in San Diego.

items.title: Eye safety: Singapore doctors report pickleball eye injuries as U.S. data shows older players at higher risk
items.summary: The Straits Times reports that Singapore hospitals have treated pickleball eye injuries from direct ball hits, including retinal breaks that needed laser treatment and a dislocated lens implant that needed surgery, though doctors there say cases can't be counted reliably. The article cites a JAMA Ophthalmology study of U.S. emergency department data: estimated pickleball eye injuries rose from fewer than 200 in 2021 to 1,262 in 2024, 43% came from direct ball impact, and players over 50 had a 39% higher risk than younger players. Doctors advise protective eyewear and urgent eye checks after any hit; one sports scientist notes injuries are rising mainly because more people are playing.

items.title: Club shakeout: Bisnow says pickleball's retail bet is souring, a Wake Forest club is sued over rent, and CityPickle questions franchising
items.summary: Bisnow reports that some pickleball clubs that leased mall and big-box space are struggling as markets saturate, pointing to The Picklr's Oct. 9 bankruptcy filing (about $19 million in liabilities across 76 franchise locations, per Bisnow) and rents of roughly $30,000 to $50,000 a month for a 10-court club. It also notes that participation is still rising: SFIA counts more than 24 million players last year, up from nearly 20 million in 2024. The Triangle Business Journal reports a landlord has sued Pickles and Play over about $80,000 in unpaid rent at its Wake Forest, N.C. location, after the operator closed another Triangle facility earlier this year. In The Dink, CityPickle co-founder Mary Cannon argues that suburban clubs are hyper-local businesses and asks whether the franchise model adds value, since rent and labor are set locally.

items.title: The Picklr bankruptcy: judge signs interim DIP order (up to $4.365M); final hearing Nov. 10 in Dallas
items.summary: The DIP loan was the item we said was still pending yesterday. The bankruptcy court in the Northern District of Texas signed the interim DIP financing order on Oct. 21 (Dkt. 43 on the Omni Agent Solutions docket). It authorizes up to $4,365,000: $3.51 million in new-money term loans, of which up to $900,000 can be borrowed in the interim period, plus a roll-up of $850,000 in pre-petition bridge loans. Dynamus Alliance, LLC is the pre-petition bridge-loan agent. The loans get first-priority liens and superpriority administrative status, subject to a carve-out. The final DIP hearing is set for Nov. 10, 2026 at 2 p.m. CT, at 1100 Commerce St., Dallas. Objections are due Nov. 3. The order says that if no objections are filed, a final order may be entered without a hearing. Nothing in the order addresses club closures.

items.title: Screaming debate: Zane Navratil says players 'should be allowed to scream' and taunt
items.summary: Times Now reports that Zane Navratil said on Instagram that players should be allowed to scream and to taunt 'if they want.' Quotes: 'Let players act how they want and then let public opinion sort it out,' and 'We aren't role models, we're entertainers.' He argues that fans' reaction is a better penalty than losing a timeout. He points to the NFL's taunting rule ('the fans hated it') and to the UFC's trash talk as an example of how drama drives attention. Times Now notes that Navratil was criticized for yelling at an opponent during the MLP playoffs and later regretted it. This is a direct counterpoint to Jim Kloss's UPA anti-taunting proposal (warning, then loss of a timeout or challenge, then a mark), which we covered Oct. 16-21.
items.social_angle: Two-sided poll: Navratil ('let public opinion sort it out') vs. Kloss (warning, then timeout/challenge, then a mark). Use his exact quotes only, and link Times Now. Don't embed or copy his Instagram media.

items.title: Noise rules spread in Singapore: Sengkang bans pickleball on some courts and limits hours from Nov. 1; Chua Chu Kang runs a foam-ball-only trial
items.summary: Mothership reports that Sengkang Town Council will ban pickleball from Nov. 1 on courts that are too close to residential blocks or that drew enough resident votes, citing MP Abdul Muhaimin's Oct. 21 Instagram post. Where pickleball is still allowed, play is limited to 10 a.m.-7:30 p.m. Banned courts will have their pickleball lines removed and signs posted. The council says residents voted these measures the most acceptable in a survey, and that it also considered distance to homes, sound frequency and site layout. Separately, Stomp reports that Chua Chu Kang Town Council is running a six-month 'use foam balls only' trial, started Oct. 1, at the court near Block 119A Plantation Crescent in Tengah. That court is open 9:30 a.m.-8 p.m. A council spokesperson confirmed on Oct. 22 that the trial is at that one court only, and said it will be evaluated before the council decides whether to continue. Mothership notes earlier steps: Holland-Bukit Panjang's 2025 ban, 9 a.m.-9 p.m. limits in some Ang Mo Kio estates, and Mountbatten's foam-ball sessions.

At the Global Pickleball Summit in Hong Kong, JOOLA CEO Richard Lee announced a $5,000 'Growth Grant' from JOOLA and RPO for GPF and WPF member federations, for equipment, coach education and beginner clinics (Pickle361, Times Now). Eligibility details were to come at a federation session. Pickle361's account of the speech says divided governance (WPF vs. GPF, USA Pickleball vs. UPA-A paddle testing) is slowing the sport. items.title: The Picklr bankruptcy: judge enters first-day orders on joint administration, wages and schedules; DIP loan order still pending
items.summary: After Monday's first-day hearing before Judge Scott W. Everett (U.S. Bankruptcy Court, N.D. Texas, Dallas), the court entered three orders on Oct. 19: joint administration of Picklr, Inc. and Picklr Clubs Inc., with Picklr, Inc. (No. 26-34687) as the lead case (Dkt. 35); authority to pay prepetition wages and keep employee benefit programs running (Dkt. 36); and more time, to Nov. 6, for Picklr, Inc. to file its schedules and statement of financial affairs (Dkt. 37). As of the latest public docket entry we saw this morning (Dkt. 37), no interim DIP financing or cash-management order had been entered. The amended proposed interim DIP order (Dkt. 20) asks for a $4.365 million facility: $3.51 million in new-money loans (up to $900,000 during the interim period) plus an $850,000 roll-up of prepetition bridge loans. Bankruptcy Observer's docket review (AI-written, citing docket numbers) adds more. The franchisor, Picklr Franchise, Inc., did not file. The debtors say landlords sought to enforce 'nearly 40' corporate lease guarantees. Franchised clubs are run by about 77 franchisee groups. Claims are due Dec. 18 (Picklr, Inc.) and Dec. 21 (Picklr Clubs), and the 341 creditors' meeting is Nov. 18 at 8:30 a.m. CT by phone. No club-closure list has been filed.
items.social_angle: Plain-English 'what got approved Monday' card: three orders in, DIP money still waiting. Add a claims-deadline box (Dec. 18 / Dec. 21) for members and landlords. No speculation on which clubs close.

items.summary: The Oxford Eagle (Oct. 19) reports that Oxford, Miss.'s Planning Commission approved the site plan for a 24-court facility at Stone Park (423 Washington Ave.): 18 courts under a pavilion and six outdoor courts, with restrooms, an elevated spectator platform and 59 more parking spaces. Retaining-wall and build-to-line variances were also approved because of the site's roughly 28.5-foot elevation change. One resident spoke against the estimated $5 million investment. In San Antonio, the city held a ribbon-cutting Monday for two new covered, lighted courts at the Northeast Senior Center (4135 Thousand Oaks). The $850,000 project used District 10 infrastructure funds (News 4 San Antonio). KSBY reports that Paso Robles, Calif., launched a free drop-in youth pickleball program. Still pending: Brentwood, Calif.'s council held a special meeting Monday on closing Creekside Park's courts once temporary courts at Sunset Park are ready (a city transition had been announced for Oct. 26). No outcome had been reported in this sweep. Reminder: Palm Springs' Demuth Park grand opening is Wednesday, Oct. 21 at 4 p.m. local (6 p.m. CT).

items.title: Asia grassroots: Parañaque Titans repeat in the Maharlika Pilipinas Pickleball Tour; ALW thanks Malaysia after her Franklin showcase
items.summary: ABS-CBN reports that the Parañaque Titans beat the Tacloban Aces 3-1 to win the second leg of the Maharlika Pilipinas Pickleball Tour (MPPT) Invitational at the Tagaytay Velodrome. That makes them back-to-back champions of Legs 1 and 2. They lost the men's match 9-11, then won women's doubles 11-4 (SJ Lim/Fatima Amirul), Mixed 1 11-1 (Ruben Gonzales/Jess Agra) and Mixed 2 11-5 (Leander Lazaro/SJ Lim). Separately, Anna Leigh Waters posted 'Thanks Malaysia for being so kind and sweet' after the Franklin Asia showcase stop (about 11.5K Instagram likes overnight), with a matching X post. That follows Franklin Malaysia's apology over an oversold Kuala Lumpur event, which we covered Oct. 18. Philippine outlets (GMA, Interaksyon, LionhearTV) are again running stories on ALW's tour and her Dec. 9 Manila return, which we covered Oct. 16.
